descriptor: Thermal imaging and electro-optic systems for defence, fabless and export-led
lede: Tonbo Imaging makes thermal sights, gimbals and fire-control sensors for armies and has just reported a ₹183 Cr second quarter after a ₹36 Cr first quarter. The ₹250 Cr order book is smaller than at March, gross margin has dropped to 34.6% from 51%, cash flow is negative, and the stock trades near 100x earnings. Management gives no numeric guidance.

short_version.text: Q2 FY27 revenue ₹183 Cr with a 24% EBITDA margin, ₹94 Cr of platform revenue in H1, order inflow of ₹188 Cr in H1, ₹408 Cr of contracts under negotiation and a big addressable list in thermal sights and directed energy.
Two years of negative operating cash flow, working capital days of 454, order book down to ₹250 Cr, gross margin down 17 points, no guidance numbers, and little history as a listed company.
About 100x earnings and 69x EV/EBITDA; even the illustrative bull case is only about 15% above the price.

blocks.text: Tonbo Imaging designs and sells sensing, targeting and fire-control equipment for soldiers and vehicles: thermal weapon sights, night-vision binoculars, stabilised gimbals, remote weapon stations and seekers, with high-power microwave and laser systems in development. It claims 100% proprietary IP, 136 R&D engineers and about 28,000 systems in 24+ countries. It is fabless: contract manufacturers build to its design.

items.text: Thermal sights and binoculars. 56% of H1 FY27 revenue (₹123 Cr) but only ₹44.5 Cr of the order book.
Remote weapon stations, gimbals, seekers and fire control. 43% of H1 revenue (₹94 Cr) and ₹205 Cr of the order book.
Land, naval and airborne microwave systems at technology readiness level 4, plus 30 kW and 300 kW lasers in development. No revenue yet beyond subsystem orders.
Deck cites a domestic need of 100,000+ tactical units (75,000 thermal weapon sights) and 100+ directed-energy systems; these are indicative, not orders.

blocks.title: Revenue and EBITDA, ₹ Cr
blocks.caption: Company-reported EBITDA excludes other income. Revenue fell 23% in FY26; H1 FY27 is +183% on a weak H1 FY26 (₹78 Cr).

blocks.title: Net profit vs operating cash flow, ₹ Cr
blocks.caption: Profit has not turned into cash since FY24: operating cash flow was -₹247 Cr over FY25, FY26 and H1 FY27 against profit of ₹130 Cr.

blocks.note: FY24-FY26 and H1 from the company's deck (p.18, 28-30); interest cover computed as (profit before tax + finance costs) / finance costs. Borrowings include only bank debt, not leases.

items.text: Poor. Inventories ₹266 Cr and receivables ₹235 Cr against ₹9 Cr of cash and bank balances (plus ₹15 Cr in other bank balances); short-term borrowings rose to ₹147 Cr from ₹116 Cr in March, and a ₹22 Cr long-term loan was added.
₹175 Cr of equity was issued in FY25 (cash flow statement), which funded the build-up; there is no later equity line in the deck.

items.lead: One quarter does not make a trend
items.text: Q1 FY27 revenue ₹36 Cr and a ₹13 Cr EBITDA loss; Q2 ₹183 Cr and ₹44 Cr EBITDA. Management itself asks to be tracked annually.

blocks.title: Points to read in the annual report

items.text: The cash flow adds back ₹12 Cr of share-option cost in FY26 and ₹5 Cr in H1 FY27, so reported profit is after that charge.
The deck labels FY25 profit before tax as 'restated' and shows FY24 earnings per share of ₹62.61 basic against ₹13.63 diluted, a gap that suggests the share structure changed recently.

blocks.note: Screener's own figures for each company. Data Patterns, Zen Technologies and Sigma are the closest small-cap defence-electronics names; BEL is the scale incumbent, and Tonbo's customers include state-owned companies and DRDO.

items.text: Fabless, export-first (export was 66% of FY25 revenue), strong in thermal imaging and stabilised sensors. Most peers sell mainly to the Indian forces.
Revenue is a fraction of Data Patterns' or BEL's, the order book is ₹250 Cr, and ROCE of 13% is below Data Patterns and BEL.
The deck points to near-term procurement of thermal sights 'through OCPP' (50,000 units) as the chance, but names no order won.

cells: Revenue went from ₹36 Cr to ₹183 Cr in one quarter; a delay moves a whole quarter
Operating cash flow -₹48 Cr in H1; inventories and receivables doubled since September 2025
Gross margin 34.6% in H1 against 51% in FY26
Export share swung from 66% (FY25) to 6% (FY26); a few orders appear to decide each year
About 100x earnings on a profit that is lumpy and mostly in one quarter

items.name: Bull
items.text: FY28 revenue ₹1,000 Cr at 28% EBITDA margin (₹280 Cr) valued at 35x EV/EBITDA, less about ₹150 Cr net debt, on 5.72 Cr shares. Needs platform and export orders to convert and directed energy to start selling.

items.name: Base
items.text: FY28 revenue ₹700 Cr at 25% margin (₹175 Cr) at 35x, less net debt. Roughly ₹250 Cr of the order book converts plus new wins at last year's pace.

items.name: Bear
items.text: FY28 revenue ₹450 Cr at 20% margin (₹90 Cr) at 30x, less net debt. Order delays and lower margins continue.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative arithmetic on stated assumptions, not forecasts; shares are market cap ÷ price (Screener). Even the bull case sits only 15% above the current price.

At about ₹8,400 Cr the market values Tonbo at roughly 17x the last four quarters' revenue (₹504 Cr on Screener's rows). EV/EBITDA is about 69x on Screener's operating profit for the last four quarters (₹124 Cr). At a 35x multiple the price needs about ₹245 Cr of EBITDA, which is revenue of roughly ₹875 Cr at a 28% margin, about 1.7 times the last four quarters. Management has not promised that and the order book does not yet support it. This is a note on valuation, not a buy or sell call.
